nodes.name: Proof that $c_{i}=x_{i}$
nodes.statement: Assume without loss of generality that $i=1$. According to Proposition~\ref{prop:x_i is chern class of a artificial bundle}, it suffices to show $P^{\sigma_{1}}$ and $(Z\times S^1)/K$ are isomorphic principal-$S^1$ bundles over $P^{\tilde{\lambda}}=Z/K$, where the action of $K$ on $S^1$ is by first including $K$ into $T^m$, then acting with weight $-(1,0,0,...,0)$. The base spaces are identified by Proposition~\ref{prop: DJ construction is OK for sym orb}. Fixing a splitting $\alpha : T^k\rightarrow T^m$, such that \begin{equation} \pi\circ\alpha=id_{T^k}. \end{equation} Define \begin{eqnarray*} f: & P^{\sigma_{1}} & \rightarrow (Z\times S^1)/K \\ & [t_{k},e^{i\theta},p] & \mapsto [\alpha(t_{k}).u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p)-\eta), \alpha(t_{k}).e^{i\theta}], \end{eqnarray*} where $t_{k}\in T^k, \theta\in \R, p\in P$, and $u_{0}: (\R_{\geq 0})^{m}\rightarrow (\R_{\geq 0})^{m}$ is given by $(z_1,\cdots,z_m)\mapsto (z_1^2,\cdots, z_m^2)$. The verification that this map is well-defined is routine. It is easy to see this map lifts the identity map of the base space, is $S^1$-equivariant and non-trivial on each fiber. So $P^{\sigma_{1}}$ and $(Z\times S^1)/K$ are isomorphic, hence $c_{1}=x_{1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Exhibit an explicit isomorphism of principal $S^1$-bundles $P^{\sigma_{1}}\cong (Z\times S^1)/K$ over $Z/K$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: the Poincar\'e dual class $D_{i}$
nodes.statement: The set $(T^k\times\tilde{F_{i}})/\tilde{\Delta}$ is a submanifold of $N$. It is the pre-image of $\tilde{F_{i}}$ under the moment map $\nu$ as defined in \eqref{eq:moment map}. Its Poincare dual, by definition, is a cohomology class in $H^{2}(N;\R)$. We denote it by $D_{i}$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: $D_{i}=-c_{i}=-x_{i}$
nodes.statement: The class $D_{i}$ equals $-c_{i}=-x_{i}$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds
conclusions: The class $D_{i}$ equals $-c_{i}=-x_{i}$.

nodes.name: Bott-Tu criterion for the first Chern class via a transversal section
nodes.statement: According to Proposition 12.8 in \cite{BT:book}, it suffices to find a transversal section of this line bundle, such that the zero locus of the section is exactly $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_{1}})$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds
nodes.origin_citation: Bott & Tu, Differential forms in algebraic topology, Proposition 12.8
conclusions: it suffices to find a transversal section of this line bundle, such that the zero locus of the section is exactly $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_{1}})$

nodes.name: Proof that $D_{i}=-x_{i}$
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, assume $i=1$. It is obvious that $-c_{1}$ is the first Chern class of the complex line bundle \begin{equation} (Z\times \C)/K\rightarrow Z/K, \end{equation} where $K$, as a subgroup of $T^m$, acts on $\C$ with weight $(1,0,0,...,0)$. According to Proposition 12.8 in \cite{BT:book}, it suffices to find a transversal section of this line bundle, such that the zero locus of the section is exactly $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_{1}})$. Define a section \begin{eqnarray*} s: &Z/K & \rightarrow (Z\times \C)/K\\ & [z_{1},z_{2},...,z_{m}]&\mapsto [(z_{1},z_{2},...,z_{m}),z_{1}], \end{eqnarray*} noticing that $Z$ is a subset of $\C^m$. It is easy to see this map is well-defined, and it is straightforward to show that \begin{equation} z_{1}=0 \Leftrightarrow \nu([z_{1},...,z_{m}])\in \tilde{F_{1}}. \end{equation} Finally, to see it is transversal to the zero section, simply notice it is holomorphic and obviously not tangent to the zero section along the zero locus.
nodes.statement_short: Take the tautological section $[z]\mapsto[(z),z_1]$, whose transversal zero locus is $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_1})$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: the generators $y_{i}$ of Tolman-Weitsman
nodes.statement: Now \begin{equation}H^{*}((EK\times ET^k)\times_{T^m}\C^m) = \Z[y_{1},...,y_{m}],\end{equation} where $y_{i}$ is the Chern class of the principal $S^1$-bundle \begin{equation} (EK\times ET^k)\times_{T^m}(\C^m\times S^1)\rightarrow (EK\times ET^k)\times_{T^m}\C^m, \end{equation} where $T^m$ acts on $S^1$ with weight $-(0,0,...,0,1,0,...,0)$, where the only $1$ is on the $i^{th}$ position.
nodes.statement_short: $y_i$ is the Chern class of the weight $-e_i$ circle bundle over $(EK\times ET^k)\times_{T^m}\C^m$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds
nodes.origin_citation: Tolman & Weitsman, The cohomology rings of symplectic quotients, Theorem 7

nodes.name: The Tolman-Weitsman generators agree with $x_{i}$
nodes.statement: The generators for the cohomology ring of a symplectic toric manifold in Theorem 7 in \cite{TW:quotients} are the same as the ones used in Theorem~\ref{thm:symp orbi cohomology} in this paper.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds
conclusions: The generators for the cohomology ring of a symplectic toric manifold in Theorem 7 in \cite{TW:quotients} are the same as the ones used in Theorem~\ref{thm:symp orbi cohomology} in this paper.

nodes.name: Restrict the moment map to the positive orthant
nodes.statement: If we restrict the domain of $u$ defined in \eqref{eq:std moment contact} to \begin{equation}(\R^m)^{+}=\{(z_{1},...,z_{m})\in \C^m: z_{i}\in \R_{\geq 0},\forall i\},\end{equation} it is a homeomorphism onto its image. Call this restriction map $u_{0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict $u$ to the nonnegative real orthant, where it is a homeomorphism onto its image.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Define the map $\gamma_{0}$
nodes.statement: Now define a map \begin{equation}\gamma_{0}: T^n\times C_{0}\rightarrow S\end{equation} by: \[(t_{n},p)\mapsto t_{n}.[u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p))]\]
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Check $\gamma_{0}$ is well defined
nodes.statement: We note that $\pi^{*}(p)\in (\R^m)^{+}$ because of the defining equations for $C$. Thus, $u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p))$ is well-defined, and it is straightforward to check that \begin{equation*}u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p))\in (i^{*}\circ u)^{-1}(0)\backslash \{0\}.\end{equation*} We let $[u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p))]\in S$ be the equivalence class of $u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p))$. Finally, $t_{n}\in T^n$ acts on $S$ as noted earlier.
nodes.statement_short: Verify $u_0^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p))$ lands in the zero level set minus the origin.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Continuity and surjectivity of $\gamma_{0}$
nodes.statement: This map $\gamma_{0}$ is a continuous. It is also surjective because $C_{0}$ is the orbit space of the $T^n$-action on $S$.
nodes.statement_short: $\gamma_0$ is continuous and surjective since $C_0$ is the orbit space.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Descend $\gamma_{0}$ to a $T^n$-equivariant homeomorphism
nodes.statement: According to Lemma~\ref{lemma:stabilizer}, which will be stated and proved right after this proposition, $\gamma_{0}$ induces a bijective map \begin{equation} \gamma: (T^n\times C_{0})/\Delta\rightarrow S\end{equation} The inverse of this map is also continuous since $\gamma$ is an open map. Finally, $\gamma$ is obviously $T^n$-equivariant.
nodes.statement_short: The stabilizer lemma makes the induced $\gamma$ bijective, open, and equivariant.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Symplectization splits as $M\times\R$
nodes.statement: By definition, the symplectic cone $S$ is the symplectization of $M$. Topologically, $S= M\times \R$. The map $\nu$ defined in \eqref{eq:moment toric } is proportional on the second coordinate.
nodes.statement_short: Use $S=M\times\R$ with $\nu$ proportional in the $\R$ coordinate.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Choose the level $x(q)$ over each point of $M$
nodes.statement: For each $q\in M$, there is a unique $x=x(q)\in \R$, such that $$\nu(q,x(q))\in P .$$
nodes.statement_short: Pick the unique scaling $x(q)$ landing in $P$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Identify $P^{\lambda}$ with the graph of $x(q)$
nodes.statement: Notice that $P^{\lambda}=(T^n\times P)/\Delta$ is a subset of $(T^n\times C_{0})/\Delta$, so $(T^n\times P)/\Delta$ is $T^n$-equivariantly homeomorphic to its image under $\gamma$ as defined in \eqref{eq:gamma}. This is precisely the pre-image of $P$ under $\nu$, which is $$\{(q,x(q))\in S=M\times \R : q\in M\}.$$ This is clearly $T^n$-equivariantly homeomorphic to $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Transport $P^{\lambda}$ by $\gamma$ onto $\nu^{-1}(P)$, a graph over $M$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: The $K$-action on $P^{\mu}$ is free
nodes.statement: The group $K$ acts naturally on $P^{\mu}=(T^m\times P)/\Omega$ by multiplication on the first coordinate. Since $C$ is a good cone, $K\cap \Omega_{p}=1$ for every $p\in P$. Thus the $K$ action on $P^{\mu}$ is free.
nodes.statement_short: Goodness of $C$ gives $K\cap\Omega_p=1$, so $K$ acts freely.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Identify the orbit space
nodes.statement: The orbit space is exactly $P^{\lambda}=(T^n\times P)/\Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: The orbit space is $P^{\lambda}$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Write down the projection $\pi'$
nodes.statement: The projection from the total space to the orbit space is given by the natural map \begin{eqnarray*}\pi':& P^{\mu}=(T^m\times P)/\Omega&\rightarrow P^{\lambda}=(T^n\times P)/\Delta\\ &[t_{m},p]&\mapsto [\pi_{T}(t_{m}),p].
nodes.statement_short: The bundle map is $[t_m,p]\mapsto[\pi_T(t_m),p]$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Set up the lattice-level sequence
nodes.statement: Consider the maps\[\xymatrix{ 0 \ar[r]^{} & ker(\pi_{\Z}) \ar[r]^{j} & \Z^m \ar[r]^{\pi_{\Z}} & \Z^n },\] where $\pi_{\Z}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:pi_Z contact} and $j$ is the inclusion map.
nodes.statement_short: Work with $0\to\ker\pi_\Z\to\Z^m\to\Z^n$ at the lattice level.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Put the inclusion $j$ in Smith normal form
nodes.statement: As a subgroup of the free abelian group $\Z^m$, $ker(\pi_{\Z})$ is also a free abelian group. So with suitably chosen basis, the map $j$ looks like an inclusion \[b_{1}\Z\oplus b_{2}\Z\oplus \cdot\cdot\cdot \oplus b_{k}\Z \hookrightarrow \Z\oplus\Z\oplus \cdot\cdot\cdot \Z\oplus \Z^{m-k}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Choose bases so that $j$ becomes $\bigoplus b_i\Z\hookrightarrow\Z^m$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Show all elementary divisors are $1$
nodes.statement: But notice that for every $x\in \Z^m$ and every $t\in \Z\backslash\{0\}$, \[x\in ker(\pi_{\Z})\Leftrightarrow tx\in ker(\pi_{\Z}).\] So all of the $b_{i}$ must be $1$.
nodes.statement_short: Saturation of $\ker\pi_\Z$ forces every $b_i=1$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Exponentiate the lattice retraction
nodes.statement: This means $ker(\pi_{\Z})$ is a direct summand of $\Z^m$, so there is a group homomorphism \begin{equation} r_{0}:\Z^m\rightarrow ker(\pi_{\Z}),\end{equation} such that \[r_{0}\circ j = id_{ker(\pi_{\Z})}.\] This $r_{0}$ induces a map \begin{equation} r: T^m\rightarrow K_{0} \end{equation} that satisfies the requirement of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: The direct-summand retraction $r_0$ induces the desired $r:T^m\to K_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Define the projection between Borel constructions
nodes.statement: Define the projection map by \[[x,y,[t,p]]\mapsto [y,[\pi(t),p]],\] where $x\in EK_{0}$, $y\in ET^n$, $t\in T^m$, $p\in P$. The square brackets $[\ ]$ are used whenever there is a equivalence relation involved.
nodes.statement_short: Send $[x,y,[t,p]]\mapsto[y,[\pi(t),p]]$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Normalize a point in the fiber
nodes.statement: It is easily shown that the map is well-defined. As for the fiber, pick any point $[y_{0},[t_{n},p]]$ in the base space, with $y_{0}\in ET^n$, $t_{n}\in T^n$, $p\in P$. Assume $[x,y,[t,p]]$ is in the pre-image, then \[[y,[\pi(t),p]]=[y_{0},[t_{n},p]].\] So there exists $s\in T^n$ such that \[sy=y_{0},\ \ \ \mbox{and}\] \[[s\cdot\pi(t),p]=[t_{n},p].\] Since $\pi_{T}$ is surjective, so there is an $s'\in T^m$ such that $\pi(s')=s$. Then \[[x,y,[t,p]]=[r(s')x,\pi(s')y,[s't,p]]=[r(s')x, y_{0}, [s't,p]],\ \mbox{and}\] \[ \pi'[(s't),p]=[\pi(s')\pi(t),p]= [s\cdot\pi(t),p]= [t_{n},p],\] where $\pi'$ is defined in Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberK}.
nodes.statement_short: Use surjectivity of $\pi_T$ to move any preimage point to a normalized representative.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Reduce to representatives with fixed $y_{0}$
nodes.statement: This means when considering the fiber over $[y_{0},[t_{n},p]]$, we only need to use representatives of the form $[x,y_{0},[t,p]],$ where $y_{0}$ is fixed, and $\pi'[t,p]= [t_{n},p]$.
nodes.statement_short: Only representatives $[x,y_0,[t,p]]$ with $\pi'[t,p]=[t_n,p]$ matter.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Identify the fiber with $EK_{0}$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberK}, we know that the set of points $[t,p]\in P^{\lambda}$ that satisfy $\pi'[t,p]=[t_{n},p]$ is homeomorphic to $K$. The elements in $T^m$ that fix $y_{0}$ are $K$. So the fiber over $[y,[t_{n},p]]$ is homeomorphic to $(EK_{0}\times K)/K$, which is homeomorphic to $EK_{0}$ via the map \[[x,k]\mapsto r(k)^{-1}x,\] noticing that $K$ acts on $EK_{0}$ by first mapping $k\in K$ to $r(k)\in K_{0}$, then applying $r(k)$ to $EK_{0}$.
nodes.statement_short: The fiber is $(EK_0\times K)/K\cong EK_0$ via $[x,k]\mapsto r(k)^{-1}x$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Introduce the interpolating space $W$
nodes.statement: Let $W= EK_{0}\times ET^n\times ET^m$. An element $t_{m}\in T^m$ acts on $W$ by the diagonal action of $(r(t_{m}), \pi(t_{m}), t_{m})$.
nodes.statement_short: Let $W=EK_0\times ET^n\times ET^m$ with the diagonal $T^m$-action.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: First projection $p_{1}$ has contractible fiber
nodes.statement: The projection \begin{equation} p_{1}: W\times_{T^m}(T^m\times P)/\Omega \rightarrow ET^m\times_{T^m}(T^m\times P)/\Omega \end{equation} is a fiber bundle with fiber $EK_{0}\times ET^n$, which is contractible, so \begin{equation} W\times_{T^m}(T^m\times P)/\Omega\stackrel{h.e.}{\sim} ET^m\times_{T^m}(T^m\times P)/\Omega , \end{equation} where $\stackrel{h.e.}{\sim}$ stands for `homotopy equivalent'.
nodes.statement_short: $p_1$ is a bundle with contractible fiber $EK_0\times ET^n$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: The diagonal $T^m$-action is free
nodes.statement_short: Split on $t_m\in K$ or $t_m\in\Omega_p$; since $K\cap\Omega_p=1$ the action is free.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Second projection $p_{2}$ has contractible fiber
nodes.statement: So the projection \begin{equation} p_{2}: W\times_{T^m}(T^m\times P)/\Omega \rightarrow (EK_{0}\times ET^n)\times_{T^m} (T^m\times P)/\Omega \end{equation} is a fiber bundle with fiber $ET^m$. So \begin{equation} W\times_{T^m}(T^m\times P)/\Omega \stackrel{h.e.}{\sim} (EK_{0}\times ET^n)\times_{T^m} (T^m\times P)/\Omega.
nodes.statement_short: $p_2$ is a bundle with contractible fiber $ET^m$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Combine the two equivalences
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:p1} and \eqref{eq:p2} completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Chain the two homotopy equivalences.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Replace the Borel construction using the $EK_{0}$-bundle lemma
nodes.statement: According to Lemma~\ref{lemma:EK0 bundle},\[H_{T^n}^{*}(M;\Z)=H^{*}(ET^n\times_{T^n} P^{\lambda},\Z)= H^{*}((EK_{0}\times ET^n)\times_{T^m}P^{\mu};\Z)\]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $H^{*}_{T^n}(M)$ as the cohomology of $(EK_0\times ET^n)\times_{T^m}P^{\mu}$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Replace it again using the homotopy equivalence lemma
nodes.statement: According to Lemma~\ref{lemma:AG Property}, they are equal to \[H_{T^m}^{*}(P^{\mu};\Z).\]
nodes.statement_short: Identify that with $H^{*}_{T^m}(P^{\mu};\Z)$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Quote the Davis-Januszkiewicz computation
nodes.statement: Then Theorem~\ref{theorem:equivariant cohomology contact} follows from Theorem 4.8 in \cite{DJ}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 4.8 of Davis-Januszkiewicz.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Set up the Borel fibration spectral sequence
nodes.statement: Consider the spectral sequence of the fiber bundle \begin{equation} M\hookrightarrow ET^n\times_{T^n}M \rightarrow BT^n \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use the Serre spectral sequence of $M\to ET^n\times_{T^n}M\to BT^n$.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Rule out torsion in $H^{1}(M;\Z)$
nodes.statement: If $E_{2}^{0,1}=H^{1}(M;\Z)$ has torsion, it will be in the kernel of \begin{equation} d_{2}: E_{2}^{0,1}\rightarrow E_{2}^{2,0} \end{equation} since $E_{2}^{2,0}=H^{2}(BT^n;\Z)=\Z^n$ is free. So the torsion part will live to $E_{\infty}^{0,1}$. Thus $H^{1}(ET^n\times_{T^n}M;\Z)$ will have torsion and contradicts Theorem~\ref{theorem:equivariant cohomology contact}, from which it easily follows that $H^{1}(ET^n\times_{T^n}M;\Z)=0$. So $H^{1}(M;\Z)$ is torsion-free.
nodes.statement_short: Torsion would survive to $E_\infty$ and contradict the equivariant computation.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Rule out a free part via $\pi_{1}(M)$
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.1 in \cite{L:homotopy group} tells us that $\pi_{1}(M)$ is a finite group. So $H_{1}(M;\Z)$ is finite, and $H^{1}(M;\Z)$ has no free part.
nodes.statement_short: Finiteness of $\pi_1(M)$ makes $H_1(M;\Z)$ finite.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Conclude $H^{1}(M;\Z)=0$
nodes.statement: Thus, we may conclude that $H^{1}(M;\Z)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: No torsion and no free part leaves zero.
nodes.section: 3 Equivariant cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Degenerate the spectral sequence of $ET^r\times_{T^r}N$
nodes.statement: The spectral sequence of the singular cohomology with $\Z$ coefficients of the fiber bundle \begin{equation*} N\hookrightarrow ET^r\times_{T^r}N\rightarrow BT^r \end{equation*} degenerates at the $E^{2}$ term, since both $N$ and $BT^r$ have cohomology only in even degrees. Thus $ET^r\times_{T^r} N$ also has cohomology only in even degrees.
nodes.statement_short: Even-degree cohomology of $N$ and $BT^r$ forces $E_2$-degeneration.
nodes.section: 4 Cohomology and equivariant cohomology of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Introduce the complementary subtorus $T^{k-r}$
nodes.statement: Denote by $T^{k-r}$ the subgroup of $T^k$ that is the product of the first $k-r$ copies of $S^1$ in $T^k= (S^1)^k$.
nodes.statement_short: Let $T^{k-r}$ be the first $k-r$ circle factors.
nodes.section: 4 Cohomology and equivariant cohomology of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Apply the Davis-Januszkiewicz argument to the residual bundle
nodes.statement: We complete the proof by applying the argument in Theorem 4.14 in \cite{DJ} to the fiber bundle \begin{equation*} ET^r\times_{T^r}N \hookrightarrow ET^{k-r}\times_{T^{k-r}}(ET^r\times_{T^r}N)\rightarrow BT^{k-r} \end{equation*} and also noticing that $ET^{k-r}\times_{T^{k-r}}(ET^r\times_{T^r}N)=ET^k\times_{T^k}N$.
nodes.statement_short: Run Theorem 4.14 of Davis-Januszkiewicz on the $T^{k-r}$-bundle.
nodes.section: 4 Cohomology and equivariant cohomology of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Fix the notation $\vec{a}=(0,\dots,0,1)$
nodes.statement_short: Name $\vec{a}=(0,\dots,0,1)$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Implication (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2)
nodes.statement: (\ref{item: def of A})$\Rightarrow$(\ref{item: dual cone}): For any $x\in C_{0}, \langle \vec{a}, x\rangle =x_{n} > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: If $C_0$ is in the upper half space then $\vec{a}$ pairs positively with $C_0$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Implication (2) $\Rightarrow$ (3)
nodes.statement: (\ref{item: dual cone})$\Rightarrow$(\ref{item:linear combi}): The dual cone $C^{\vee}$ is spanned by rays along $v_{1},v_{2},...,v_{m}$. So any vector in the interior of it can be expressed as linear combination of $\{v_{i},1\leq i\leq m\}$ with positive coefficients.
nodes.statement_short: Interior points of the dual cone are positive combinations of its spanning rays $v_i$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Implication (3) $\Rightarrow$ (1)
nodes.statement: (\ref{item:linear combi})$\Rightarrow$(\ref{item: def of A}): For any $x\in C$, we have $\langle x, v_{i}\rangle \geq 0$, for $1\leq i\leq m$, with all equalities if and only if $x=\vec{0}$. Suppose \begin{equation*} \vec{a}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}k_{i}v_{i}, \mbox{with}\ k_{i}>0\ \forall i.\end{equation*} Then \begin{equation*}x_{n}=\langle x, \vec{a}\rangle= \sum_{i=1}^{m}k_{i}\langle x, v_{i}\rangle \geq 0.\end{equation*} The equality holds if and only if $x=\vec{0}$. So for any $x\in C_{0}, x_{n}>0$, i.e., $C_{0}\subset U\R^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Expanding $x_n=\langle x,\vec{a}\rangle$ as a positive combination gives $x_n>0$ off the origin.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Choose $D$ sending the primitive vector to $(0,\dots,0,1)$
nodes.statement: Let $v=\sum_{i=1}^{m}v_{i}$ and $u$ be the primitive vector in the direction of $v$. Suppose \begin{equation*} u=\frac{1}{k}v, \mbox{for}\ k\in \Z_{>0}. \end{equation*} Since $u$ is primitive, there exists $D\in SL(n,\Z)$, such that, $D(u)=(0,0,...,0,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $u$ primitive along $\sum_i v_i$ and $D\in SL(n,\Z)$ with $D(u)=(0,\dots,0,1)$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Define the transformation $B=D^{T}$
nodes.statement: Define a transformation $B$ of $\R^n$ by: \begin{equation} x\mapsto Bx= D^{T}x , \end{equation} where the matrix for $D^{T}$ is the transpose of the matrix for $D$. Since $det D^{T}=det D=1$, we still have $B\in SL(n;\Z)$.
nodes.statement_short: Set $B=D^{T}$, still in $SL(n;\Z)$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Compute the normals of the transformed cone
nodes.statement: Under this transformation $B$, the cone $C = \bigcup_{i=1}^{m}\{x\in \R^n: \langle x, v_{i}\rangle \geq 0\}$ is taken to \begin{equation}B(C)= \bigcup_{i=1}^{m}\{x\in \R^n: \langle x, D(v_{i})\rangle \geq 0\}.\end{equation} So the normal vectors to the facets of the new cone $B(C)$ are $\{D(v_{i}):1\leq i\leq m\}$. Moreover, \begin{equation} (0,0,...,0,1)=D(u)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{1}{k}D(v_{i}).
nodes.statement_short: The new facet normals are $D(v_i)$ and $(0,\dots,0,1)$ is their positive combination.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Apply the equivalence lemma
nodes.statement: Finally, using Lemma~\ref{lemma:equiva of Assu A}, we see that the new cone $B(C_{0})$ is in $U\R^n$.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (3) of the lemma now gives $B(C_0)\subset U\R^n$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: The last circle acts freely on $M$
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} S^1=\{(1,1,...,1,e^{i\theta_{n}})\in T^n: \theta_{n}\in \R\} \end{equation} act on $M=(T^n\times P)/\Delta$ by multiplication on $T^n$. Because of the smoothness criterion we imposed, $S^1\cap \Delta_{p}=1$, for any $p\in P$, and so this action is free.
nodes.statement_short: The smoothness criterion gives $S^1\cap\Delta_p=1$, so the action is free.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Compute the quotient
nodes.statement: The quotient space is \begin{equation} (T^n\times P)/\langle \Delta, S^1\rangle = (T^n\times P)/\langle \widetilde{\Delta}, S^1 \rangle = (T^n/S^1\times P)/\widetilde{\Delta} = (T^{n-1}\times P)/\widetilde{\Delta}.
nodes.statement_short: Collapsing $S^1$ turns $(T^n\times P)/\Delta$ into $(T^{n-1}\times P)/\widetilde{\Delta}$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Read off the projection
nodes.statement: Therefore $N$ is the orbit space, and from the construction, we can see the map from the space $M$ to $N$ just drops the last coordinate of $t$.
nodes.statement_short: The bundle map just drops the last torus coordinate.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Even part from exactness at the right end
nodes.statement: The isomorphism \eqref{eq:H_e} follows from the exactness of \eqref{eq:grouped ses} at the second $H^{*}(N;\Z)$ and $H^{even}(M;\Z)$ and also the fact that $d^{*}: H^{*}(N;\Z)\rightarrow H^{even}(M;\Z)$ is a ring homomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Exactness plus multiplicativity of $d^{*}$ gives the ring isomorphism with $coker\rho$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: $d_{*}$ is a module homomorphism
nodes.statement: As for \eqref{eq:H_o}, first notice that it follows from \eqref{eq:push-pull} that the map \begin{equation} d_{*}: H^{odd}(M;\Z)\rightarrow H^{*}(N;\Z) \end{equation} is a $H^{*}(N;\Z)$-module homomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: The push-pull formula makes $d_{*}$ $H^{*}(N;\Z)$-linear.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Odd part from exactness at the left end
nodes.statement: Exactness of \eqref{eq:grouped ses} at $H^{odd}(M;\Z)$ and the first $H^{2k}(N;\Z)$ shows that \begin{equation} d_{*}: H^{odd}(M;\Z)\rightarrow ker\rho \end{equation} is an $H^{*}(N;\Z)$-module isomorphism, hence an $H^{*}(N;\Z)/\langle e\rangle$-module isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Exactness identifies $H^{odd}(M;\Z)$ with $\ker\rho$ as modules.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Pull-back along the inclusion $f_{1}$
nodes.statement: The map $f_{1}$ is an inclusion, so the pull back of $L_{1}$ by $f_{1}$ is just by restriction. Then the equation \eqref{eq:f_1} follows from the definition.
nodes.statement_short: $f_1^{*}L_1=M$ because $f_1$ is an inclusion of the fiber.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Reduce to constructing an equivariant map
nodes.statement: To show \eqref{eq:L_2}, it's enough if we can construct an $S^1$-equivariant map from $f_{3}^{*}L_{3}$ to $f_{2}^{*}L_{1}$ , which lifts the identity map of the base space $(E\tilde{K}\times ET^{n-1})\times_{T^m}P^{\mu}$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to build an $S^1$-equivariant map over the identity of the base.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Fix a point $q$ of the base space
nodes.statement: Let $q= [x,y,[e^{i\vec{\theta}},p]]$ be a point in the base space $(E\tilde{K}\times ET^{n-1})\times_{T^m}P^{\mu}$, where $x\in E\tilde{K}, y\in ET^{n-1}, \vec{\theta}=(\theta_{1},...,\theta_{m}), e^{i\vec{\theta}}=(e^{i\theta_{1}},...,e^{i\theta_{m}})\in T^m$, and $p\in P$.
nodes.statement_short: Write a base point as $q=[x,y,[e^{i\vec\theta},p]]$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Compute the two fibers over $q$
nodes.statement: The fiber of $f_{3}^{*}L_{3}$ over the point $q$ is, by the definition of pull-back, the fiber of $L_{3}$ over the point $f_{3}(q)=[(x,y),pt]$, namely \begin{equation} f_{3}^{*}L_{3}|_{q}=\{[(x,y), e^{i\beta}]:\beta\in \R\}. \end{equation} The fiber of $f_{2}^{*}L_{1}$ over the point $q$ is, by the definition of pull-back, the fiber of $L_{1}$ over the point $f_{2}(q)=[y,[ \tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\theta}}),p]]$, namely \begin{equation} f_{2}^{*}L_{1}|_{q}=\{[y,[(\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\theta}}),e^{i\alpha}),p]]: \alpha\in \R\}.
nodes.statement_short: Write out $f_3^{*}L_3|_q$ and $f_2^{*}L_1|_q$ by the definition of pull-back.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Define the fibrewise map $s_{q}$
nodes.statement: Define a map from $f_{3}^{*}L_{3}|_{q}$ to $f_{2}^{*}L_{1}|_{q}$ by sending \begin{equation} [x,y, e^{i\beta}]\mapsto [y,[(\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\theta}}),e^{i\beta+i\langle \vec{v^{l}},\vec{\theta}\rangle}),p]]. \end{equation} We call this map $s_{q}$. To show $s_{q}$ is well-defined, we need to show the definition is independent of the choice of representative of $q$.
nodes.statement_short: Twist the fiber coordinate by $e^{i\langle\vec{v^l},\vec\theta\rangle}$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: First representative check: translation by $e^{i\vec{\phi}}\in T^m$
nodes.statement: First, assume $e^{i\vec{\phi}}\in T^m$, and so \begin{equation} [x,y,[e^{i\vec{\theta}},p]]=[\tilde{r}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})x,\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})y,[e^{i(\vec{\theta}+\vec{\phi})},p]]. \end{equation} Using this representative of $q$, then \begin{eqnarray*} s_{q}([x,y,e^{i\beta}])& = & s_{q}([\tilde{r}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})x,\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})y, e^{i(\beta+\langle -\vec{v^{l}},\vec{\phi}\rangle)}])\\ & = & [\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})y,[(\tilde{\pi}(e^{i(\vec{\theta}+\vec{\phi})}),e^{i\beta-i\langle \vec{v^{l}},\vec{\phi}\rangle +i\langle\vec{v^{l}},(\vec{\theta}+\vec{\phi}) \rangle}),p]]\\ & = & [\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})y,[(\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\phi}})\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\theta}}),e^{i\beta+i\langle \vec{v^{l}},\vec{\theta}\rangle}),p]]. \end{eqnarray*} This equals to the RHS of \eqref{eq:3} by the definition of $L_{1}$ as given before Lemma~\ref{lemma:digram Euler}.
nodes.statement_short: Changing the representative by a torus element leaves $s_q$ unchanged.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Second representative check: translation by $e^{i\vec{\delta}}\in\Omega_{p}$
nodes.statement: Second, choose a different representative by letting $e^{i\vec{\delta}}\in \Omega_{p}$, and then \begin{equation} [x,y,[e^{i\vec{\theta}},p]]=[x,y,[e^{i\vec{\delta}}e^{i\vec{\theta}},p]]. \end{equation} Using this representative of $q$, we have: \begin{eqnarray*} s_{q}([(x,y),e^{i\beta}]) & = & [y,[(\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\delta}}e^{i\vec{\theta}}),e^{i\beta+i\langle \vec{v^{l}},\vec{\delta}+\vec{\theta}\rangle}),p]]\\ & = & [y,[(\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\delta}})\cdot\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\theta}}),e^{i\langle\vec{v^l},\vec{\delta}\rangle}\cdot e^{i\beta+i\langle\vec{v^l},\vec{\theta}\rangle}),p]]. \end{eqnarray*} This also equals to the RHS of \eqref{eq:3} since \begin{equation} (\tilde{\pi}(e^{i\vec{\delta}}),e^{i\langle\vec{v^l},\vec{\delta}\rangle})\in \Delta_{p}, \end{equation} which is true by definition of $\Delta, \widetilde{\Delta}$ and $\vec{v^l}$.
nodes.statement_short: Changing it by an element of $\Omega_p$ also leaves $s_q$ unchanged, since $(\tilde\pi(e^{i\vec\delta}),e^{i\langle\vec{v^l},\vec\delta\rangle})\in\Delta_p$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Conclude well-definedness and equivariance
nodes.statement: So the map $s_{q}$ defined by \eqref{eq:3} is well-defined. It's obviously $S^{1}$-equivariant.
nodes.statement_short: $s_q$ is well defined and $S^1$-equivariant, giving the bundle isomorphism.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Quote Guillemin's formula for the K\"ahler class
nodes.statement: According to Theorem 6.3 in \cite{Guillemin:Kaehler form}, the cohomology class of the K$\ddot{a}$hler form on $N$ is given by \begin{equation} [\omega]=2\pi\sum_{i=1}^{m}v_{in}D_{i}, \end{equation} where $D_{i}$ denotes the cohomology class in $H^{2}(N;\R)$ that is the Poincare dual to $(T^{n-1}\times \tilde{F_{i}})/\tilde{\Delta}$.
nodes.statement_short: $[\omega]=2\pi\sum_i v_{in}D_i$ on $N$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Substitute $D_{i}=-x_{i}$ to get $[\omega]=-2\pi e$
nodes.statement: According to Proposition~\ref{prop:Poincare dual} in the Appendix, $D_{i}=-x_{i}$. So \begin{equation} [\omega]=-2\pi e.
nodes.statement_short: The appendix identifies $D_i=-x_i$, so the K\"ahler class is $-2\pi e$.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Apply Hard Lefschetz over $\Q$
nodes.statement: Using the Hard Lefschetz Theorem on $N$, it follows easily from Theorem~\ref{thm:contact cohomology} that \begin{equation}H^{2k+1}(M;\Q)=0 \end{equation} for $\{k\in \N: 1\leq 2k+1\leq n-1\}$, and \begin{equation} H^{2k}(M;\Q)=0 \end{equation} for $\{k\in \N:n\leq 2k\leq 2n-2\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Hard Lefschetz on $N$ gives the rational vanishing ranges.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Upgrade from $\Q$ to $\Z$ by torsion-freeness
nodes.statement: Furthermore, as the cohomology ring of a symplectic toric manifold, the ring $\Z[x_{1},x_{2},...,x_{m}]/\{\I,\tilde{\J}\}$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:contact cohomology} is torsion-free (see \cite{toric variety}). Therefore as an ideal of it, $ker\rho$ is also torsion-free. Hence \begin{equation}H^{2k+1}(M;\Z)=0 \end{equation} for $\{k\in \N: 1\leq 2k+1\leq n-1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\ker\rho$ is torsion-free, so the odd vanishing holds integrally.
nodes.section: 5 The singular cohomology of good contact toric manifolds

nodes.name: Reduce to $i=1$ and to a bundle isomorphism
nodes.statement: Assume without loss of generality that $i=1$. According to Proposition~\ref{prop:x_i is chern class of a artificial bundle}, it suffices to show $P^{\sigma_{1}}$ and $(Z\times S^1)/K$ are isomorphic principal-$S^1$ bundles over $P^{\tilde{\lambda}}=Z/K$, where the action of $K$ on $S^1$ is by first including $K$ into $T^m$, then acting with weight $-(1,0,0,...,0)$. The base spaces are identified by Proposition~\ref{prop: DJ construction is OK for sym orb}.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to identify $P^{\sigma_1}$ with $(Z\times S^1)/K$ as $S^1$-bundles.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Construct the bundle map $f$
nodes.statement: Fixing a splitting $\alpha : T^k\rightarrow T^m$, such that \begin{equation} \pi\circ\alpha=id_{T^k}. \end{equation} Define \begin{eqnarray*} f: & P^{\sigma_{1}} & \rightarrow (Z\times S^1)/K \\ & [t_{k},e^{i\theta},p] & \mapsto [\alpha(t_{k}).u_{0}^{-1}(\pi^{*}(p)-\eta), \alpha(t_{k}).e^{i\theta}], \end{eqnarray*} where $t_{k}\in T^k, \theta\in \R, p\in P$, and $u_{0}: (\R_{\geq 0})^{m}\rightarrow (\R_{\geq 0})^{m}$ is given by $(z_1,\cdots,z_m)\mapsto (z_1^2,\cdots, z_m^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a splitting $\alpha$ and define $f[t_k,e^{i\theta},p]$ explicitly.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Check $f$ is a bundle isomorphism
nodes.statement: The verification that this map is well-defined is routine. It is easy to see this map lifts the identity map of the base space, is $S^1$-equivariant and non-trivial on each fiber. So $P^{\sigma_{1}}$ and $(Z\times S^1)/K$ are isomorphic, hence $c_{1}=x_{1}$.
nodes.statement_short: $f$ lifts the identity, is equivariant and fibrewise nontrivial, so $c_1=x_1$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Reduce to $i=1$ and identify $-c_{1}$
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, assume $i=1$. It is obvious that $-c_{1}$ is the first Chern class of the complex line bundle \begin{equation} (Z\times \C)/K\rightarrow Z/K, \end{equation} where $K$, as a subgroup of $T^m$, acts on $\C$ with weight $(1,0,0,...,0)$.
nodes.statement_short: $-c_1$ is the first Chern class of the weight $(1,0,\dots,0)$ line bundle.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Invoke the Bott-Tu transversal-section criterion
nodes.statement: According to Proposition 12.8 in \cite{BT:book}, it suffices to find a transversal section of this line bundle, such that the zero locus of the section is exactly $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_{1}})$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to find a transversal section with zero locus $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_1})$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Construct the tautological section $s$
nodes.statement: Define a section \begin{eqnarray*} s: &Z/K & \rightarrow (Z\times \C)/K\\ & [z_{1},z_{2},...,z_{m}]&\mapsto [(z_{1},z_{2},...,z_{m}),z_{1}], \end{eqnarray*} noticing that $Z$ is a subset of $\C^m$. It is easy to see this map is well-defined, and it is straightforward to show that \begin{equation} z_{1}=0 \Leftrightarrow \nu([z_{1},...,z_{m}])\in \tilde{F_{1}}.
nodes.statement_short: Take $s[z]=[(z),z_1]$, whose zero locus is $\nu^{-1}(\tilde{F_1})$.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds

nodes.name: Check transversality
nodes.statement: Finally, to see it is transversal to the zero section, simply notice it is holomorphic and obviously not tangent to the zero section along the zero locus.
nodes.statement_short: Holomorphy gives transversality to the zero section.
nodes.section: 6 Appendix: Several equivalent descriptions of the generators of cohomology rings of symplectic toric manifolds
